acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Host Ira Glass talks about the Four Corners tourist monument where Arizona, Colorado, Utah and New Mexico meet.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
Sarah Vowell has a theory that you can tell the entire history of the United States by standing on one street corner—specifically at Michigan Avenue and Wacker Drive in Chicago—and describing all the events that happened within eyeshot of the corner. She covers three centuries of history, from Louis Joliet to Keanu Reeves.
Correction: In this story, Sarah Vowell referenced The Jungle and mistakenly cited the author as Sinclair Lewis. The correct author is Upton Sinclair.
acts.title: History

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Scott Richer and Julie Riggs of Louisville, Kentucky, were supposed to have their first kiss at the corner where South Fourth Street meets the alley behind the West End Baptist Church. But it went wrong.
acts.title: Love

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Writer Mike Paterniti tells a story of dogs and a community of dogwalkers that formed on the grounds of an old cemetery at the corner of Vaughn and Clifford in Portland, Maine.
acts.title: Neighbors

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Writer Achy Obejas reads a piece of short fiction from her book, We Came All the Way from Cuba So You Could Dress Like This?

songs.t: My Little Corner of the World

acts.title: How To Become An American
